URL: https://cnbc.com/2026/10/29/gold-slips-as-markets-assess-fed-signals-await-us-inflation-data.html
CNBC 29 Oct

Gold fell to a one-year low on Friday and silver slid below $50 an ​ounce for the first time ​since November 2025 as ​higher energy prices and persistent inflation concerns strengthened expectations that US interest rates will stay high.

Spot gold was down 2.7% at $3,910.53 per ounce, its lowest since October ⁠2025. US ‌gold futures for December delivery fell 2.8% to $3,919.60 per ⁠ounce. Bullion prices are on track for a second straight monthly decline, down 5.9% so far this month.

Spot silver was down 5.8% at $49.34 per ounce, its lowest since November 2025.

"Ongoing concerns about inflation have multiple ‌central banks continuing to tilt hawkish," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals.

"Even though holds were delivered by major central ​banks this week, the indication was that the higher-for-longer theme prevails, and that's weighing on precious metals."

Major central banks hit pause on rate rises this week, but made clear the tightening cycle isn't over, with the US Federal Reserve and the ⁠European Central Bank both pointing to inflation risks from surging energy costs.

Data on Thursday showed US ‌inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for gasoline and ‌other goods, bolstering economists' expectations of a rate hike in December.

Another factor for the price decline is the sharp fall in technology stock prices, which may have led to forced selling and margin ⁠calls, analysts at Commerzbank said in a note.

"We consider the fall in precious ⁠metal prices to be exaggerated and continue to expect a recovery," they ⁠added.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq was set for steep losses at Friday's open on AI spending worries.

Meanwhile, oil prices climbed and were set for a ​fourth monthly gain. Higher energy prices strengthen expectations ‌of a prolonged period of elevated interest rates, making non-yielding assets such as gold less attractive.

Elsewhere, physical gold demand in key Asian markets remained subdued this week, with Indian buyers delaying purchases in anticipation of a further decline in prices, while demand in top consumer China stayed muted.
